programme: SALL4, UTF1, ZNF281, ID4 and ZFP64 form a reactivated embryonic stem/progenitor transcriptional module — SALL4 driving a NANOG/SOX2/KIT/ABCG2/EPCAM/CDH1/ZEB1 self-renewal-and-EMT target set, UTF1 and ZNF281 reinforcing the same undifferentiated state (UTF1 via the pluripotency-circuit gene TCF3 and FBXO15; ZNF281 via NANOG and the EMT marker VIM), ID4 blocking differentiation (via BRCA1/TP53/SOX2/IGF1R), and ZFP64 rewiring glycolytic metabolism to support the stem-like phenotype (NOTCH1 target). ISL1, a LIM-homeodomain progenitor-specifying factor, sits at the edge of this module — active in progenitor states across several tissues but its own target set (GCG/INS/SST/ARX/PITX1) is endocrine-progenitor rather than stemness-circuit in character.
role_in_a: In breast cancer, chiefly TNBC, this module marks and drives a cancer-stem-cell-like, therapy-resistant subpopulation: SALL4 sustains self-renewal and doxorubicin resistance (PMID 26935744, 41498967), UTF1 marks stemness with prognostic association (PMID 36760370, 25435811), ID4 blocks luminal differentiation to preserve a basal/stem phenotype (PMID 40640173, 40186425), ZFP64 reprograms glycolysis to support stem-like tumorigenesis (PMID 39294751), and ISL1 promotes proliferation, invasion and angiogenesis (PMID 29497310).
role_in_b: In stroke, the direct evidence for this module is thin and mostly indirect: SALL4 partners with Myocd to reprogram fibroblasts toward a progenitor-like state after cardiac injury (PMID 33718351, an injury-reprogramming analogue rather than stroke itself), ISL1-lineage progenitors require Ezh2 for normal development and embryonic motor-neuron programming factors reactivate immature gene expression after neuronal injury to suppress ALS pathology (PMID 41883246, 40796666), and ZNF281 turns up on an immune-gene list from aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (PMID 36172261). None of this is framed as ischemic-stroke disease mechanism; Open Targets carries no stroke association for SALL4, UTF1 or ZNF281, and only a low one for ISL1 (percentile 0.15).
shared_axis: Both a breast tumor and injured neurovascular/blood-forming tissue can revert cells toward an embryonic progenitor transcriptional state; in the tumor this reversion is pathogenic (self-renewal, chemoresistance, invasion), while in the injured setting the same class of factors appears in contexts of attempted regenerative reprogramming (cardiac fibroblast, motor neuron) rather than disease-driving. SALL4's discordant (rather than concordant) behavior across patient groups is consistent with the same target module being engaged in opposite directions in the two settings.
reasoning: The module is clearly nameable and several factors (SALL4, UTF1, ID4, ZFP64, ISL1) are independently and directly placed in breast cancer with mechanistic papers, so this is not a guess about what the programme is. But no retrieved paper connects the module to stroke as a disease mechanism — the stroke-side evidence is either an injury-reprogramming analogue in a different organ (heart), a neurodegeneration paper (ALS, not stroke), a hemorrhage-specific immune gene list, or absent — so the cross-disease link rests on reasoning about shared developmental-reprogramming biology, not on retrieved evidence of the pair together.
support: PMID 26935744 — SALL4 knockdown reverses doxorubicin resistance in breast cancer (also the only paper co-mentioning both diseases' contexts, but only tests breast). PMID 41498967 — SALL4-targeted peptide suppresses PD-L1 in breast cancer. PMID 33718351 — Sall4 with Myocd reprograms cardiac fibroblasts to a progenitor state after injury (stroke-adjacent, not stroke itself). PMID 36760370, 25435811 — UTF1 expression and prognostic significance in breast cancer. PMID 40640173, 40186425 — ID4 as a driver of aggression and mammary differentiation control in breast cancer. PMID 39294751 — ZFP64 drives glycolysis-mediated stemness and tumorigenesis in breast cancer. PMID 29963304 — ZFP64 in a GWAS locus list for cerebral infarction (genetic association only, no mechanism). PMID 29497310 — ISL1 upregulated, promotes proliferation/invasion/angiogenesis in breast cancer. PMID 41883246, 40796666 — Isl1-lineage progenitor development and embryonic motor-neuron programming factors reactivated after neuronal injury (CNS-adjacent, not stroke pathology directly). PMID 36172261 — ZNF281 among immune genes in subarachnoid hemorrhage.
how_to_falsify: Profile peri-infarct or peripheral blood samples from stroke patients (matching the blood tissue this network was built from) for SALL4, UTF1, ZNF281, ID4, ZFP64 and ISL1 expression; if none show injury-associated reactivation relative to controls, the 'shared reprogramming module' account fails. Complementarily, knock down SALL4 or ZFP64 in a TNBC stem-cell assay and in an ischemia/reperfusion or fibroblast-reprogramming model in parallel — if the direction of the stemness/progenitor gene-expression change is concordant rather than opposite in the two systems, that would contradict the 'opposite valence, same module' explanation for SALL4's discordant flag.
caveats: The stroke side of this network is built from blood, not brain tissue, so 'stroke' evidence here likely reflects circulating or marrow progenitor signal rather than infarct biology directly — a real limitation given the tissue pairing is blood|breast. Support spans 117 patient-group comparisons from only 4 independent cohort pairs, and the carrying factors sit at 51-71/117 (44-60%) concordance, not near-universal agreement. SALL4 is explicitly flagged discordant (56/117), meaning its target identity recurs but its direction of regulation likely differs between the diseases. One ISL1 breast-cancer paper (PMID 42099237) carries a published Expression of Concern and should be weighted down accordingly. The tissue-generic exclusion list (SPI1, IRF8, IKZF1, IRF4, STAT1, CEBPB, PRDM1, MEF2C, AR, FLI1, CIITA, E2F3) confirms that ordinary blood-immune or hematopoietic regulators were already stripped out, so this stemness/reprogramming account is not simply re-describing generic immune signal; the single-view exclusions (IRF8, E2F5, GLI1, TRIB3, CREB5, ZFHX3, NCOA1, CREBZF, PRDM1, HIF3A, HCFC1, BHLHE22) likewise offer no alternative interferon/immune story that a one-subgroup account would have relied on.
